title: Given only kp non-zero, update returns kp*error for each accepted step and the integral stays 0
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=0, kd=0
inputs: gains kp=2 ki=0 kd=0; dt_s=0.5; error sequence 3, -1.5, 0
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=0, kd=0) | 2. Call update(3, 0.5) | 3. Call update(-1.5, 0.5) | 4. Call update(0, 0.5) | 5. Read integral() after each call
expected_result: Each result has status Ok; outputs are 6, -3, 0 in order; integral() equals 0 after every call
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output (exact compare), expected values computed in the test from the formula
notes: P term of backlog CTL-01 reference response (B1). Vectors are test-only exactly representable values, not tuning gains. Comparison tolerance TBD (design decision) if inexact vectors are later used. Parent ID for the P/I/D/combined/reset/reject sub-cases below (design open question 7).

title: Given only ki non-zero and a constant error, the output ramps linearly by ki*error*dt per step
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=0, ki=2, kd=0
inputs: gains kp=0 ki=2 kd=0; dt_s=0.5; error 3 for 4 steps
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=2, kd=0) | 2. Call update(3, 0.5) four times | 3. Record each output | 4. Read integral()
expected_result: Each status is Ok; outputs are 3, 6, 9, 12 in order; integral() equals 12
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, and integral()
notes: I term of backlog CTL-01 reference response (B1, B2). Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given a ramp built from a positive error, a sign flip in the error reverses the ramp
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=0, ki=2, kd=0 and four steps of error 3 already applied (integral 12)
inputs: error -3 for 2 steps; dt_s=0.5
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=2, kd=0) | 2. Call update(3, 0.5) four times | 3. Call update(-3, 0.5) twice and record outputs | 4. Read integral()
expected_result: The last two statuses are Ok; outputs are 9 then 6; integral() equals 6
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, and integral()
notes: B2 sign behaviour. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given only kd non-zero, the first accepted step after configure gives a D term of 0 regardless of the error
preconditions: Pid freshly configured with kp=0, ki=0, kd=2
inputs: gains kp=0 ki=0 kd=2; dt_s=0.5; error 5
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=0, kd=2) | 2. Call update(5, 0.5)
expected_result: status is Ok; output equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output
notes: B3 first-step rule. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given only kd non-zero, a constant error after the first step gives a D term of 0
preconditions: Pid freshly configured with kp=0, ki=0, kd=2
inputs: gains kp=0 ki=0 kd=2; dt_s=0.5; error 3 for 3 steps
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=0, kd=2) | 2. Call update(3, 0.5) three times and record outputs
expected_result: All statuses are Ok; every output equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output for each call
notes: B1 derivative of a constant error. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given only kd non-zero and a ramp error, the output equals kd times the error slope after the first step
preconditions: Pid freshly configured with kp=0, ki=0, kd=2
inputs: gains kp=0 ki=0 kd=2; dt_s=0.5; error sequence 0, 1, 2, 3
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=0, kd=2) | 2. Call update with errors 0, 1, 2, 3 each with dt_s=0.5 | 3. Record outputs
expected_result: All statuses are Ok; outputs are 0, 4, 4, 4 in order
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output for each call
notes: D term of backlog CTL-01 reference response (B1, B3). Slope is 1 error unit per step, so kd*slope = 2*(1/0.5). Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given a step length that changes between calls, the D term is computed with the dt of the current call
preconditions: Pid freshly configured with kp=0, ki=0, kd=2
inputs: error sequence 0, 1, 2; dt_s sequence 0.5, 0.5, 0.25
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=0, kd=2) | 2. Call update(0, 0.5) | 3. Call update(1, 0.5) | 4. Call update(2, 0.25)
expected_result: Outputs are 0, 4, 8; all statuses are Ok
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output for each call
notes: B1 uses the dt passed to the current update. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given all three gains non-zero, the output equals the sum of the P, I, and D terms
preconditions: Pid freshly configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: gains kp=2 ki=4 kd=1; dt_s=0.5; error sequence 1, 3, 3
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(1, 0.5) | 3. Call update(3, 0.5) | 4. Call update(3, 0.5) | 5. Read integral() after each call
expected_result: Statuses are Ok; outputs are 4, 18, 20 in order; integral() is 2, 8, 14 in order
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, and integral(); expected sums computed in the test from separate P, I, D terms
notes: B1, B2, B3 combined. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given all gains zero, update returns Ok with output 0 and a zero integral
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=0, ki=0, kd=0
inputs: gains all 0; dt_s=0.5; error sequence 5, -5
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=0, ki=0, kd=0) | 2. Call update(5, 0.5) | 3. Call update(-5, 0.5) | 4. Read integral()
expected_result: Both statuses are Ok; both outputs equal 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, and integral()
notes: Lower boundary of the gain range: zero is finite and accepted.

title: Given accumulated integral and derivative history, reset clears both and keeps the gains
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1 and two steps applied (errors 1 then 3, dt_s=0.5)
inputs: gains kp=2 ki=4 kd=1; post-reset error 3; dt_s=0.5
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(1, 0.5) then update(3, 0.5) | 3. Call reset() | 4. Read integral(), gains(), configured() | 5. Call update(3, 0.5)
expected_result: After reset: integral() equals 0, gains() equals kp=2 ki=4 kd=1, configured() is true; the next update returns Ok with output 12 (P 6 + I 6 + D 0 because history is cleared)
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on integral(), gains(), configured(), status, and output
notes: B3, B5. Test-only exact vectors.

title: Given an unconfigured instance, reset does not make it configured and update still returns NotConfigured
preconditions: Freshly constructed Pid, never configured; second sub-check follows a rejected configure with a NaN gain
inputs: reset() calls; update(1, 0.5)
steps: 1. Construct Pid | 2. Call reset() | 3. Read configured() | 4. Call update(1, 0.5) | 5. Call configure with kp=NaN, ki=0, kd=0 | 6. Call reset() | 7. Read configured() | 8. Call update(1, 0.5)
expected_result: configured() is false at steps 3 and 7; both updates return status NotConfigured with output 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_FALSE on configured(); EXPECT_EQ on status and output
notes: reset() is not a recovery action and enables nothing (design 4.3). Pid holds no arm or failsafe state, so FR-067 is covered only as 'reset never turns an unusable controller into a usable one'; arm-path coverage is owned by STA and SAF.

title: Given a freshly constructed Pid, configure with finite gains returns Ok, stores the gains, and sets configured
preconditions: Freshly constructed Pid
inputs: gains kp=2 ki=4 kd=1
steps: 1. Construct Pid | 2. Call configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 3. Read configured(), gains(), integral()
expected_result: configure returns Ok; configured() is true; gains() equals kp=2 ki=4 kd=1; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, configured(), gains(), integral()
notes: B4. FR-047 is partial: only the finite-value check exists here; bounds and versioning are owned by CTL-04 (TC-CTRL-005).

title: Given a configured Pid with state, configure with new finite gains replaces the gains and clears the state
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1 and two steps applied
inputs: new gains kp=1 ki=0 kd=0; error 3; dt_s=0.5
steps: 1. Construct Pid, configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1), then update(1, 0.5) and update(3, 0.5) | 2. Call configure(kp=1, ki=0, kd=0) | 3. Read gains(), integral() | 4. Call update(3, 0.5)
expected_result: configure returns Ok; gains() equals kp=1 ki=0 kd=0; integral() equals 0; the update returns Ok with output 3
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, gains(), integral(), and output

title: Given a never-configured Pid, configure with a non-finite gain returns InvalidConfig and the Pid stays unconfigured
preconditions: Freshly constructed Pid
inputs: three configure calls, one per gain: kp=NaN; ki=+infinity; kd=-infinity (other gains 0)
steps: 1. Construct Pid | 2. Call configure with kp=NaN and read status and configured() | 3. Call configure with ki=+infinity and read status and configured() | 4. Call configure with kd=-infinity and read status and configured() | 5. Call update(1, 0.5)
expected_result: Each configure returns InvalidConfig; configured() stays false after each; update returns NotConfigured with output 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, EXPECT_FALSE on configured(), EXPECT_EQ on output
notes: Design 4.2 configure; finite-value check only. Gain bounds are owned by CTL-04.

title: Given a configured Pid with state, configure with a non-finite gain returns InvalidConfig and leaves gains and state unchanged
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1 and two steps applied (errors 1 then 3, dt_s=0.5; integral 8)
inputs: rejected configure: kp=NaN, ki=4, kd=1; then update(3, 0.5)
steps: 1. Construct Pid, configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1), update(1, 0.5), update(3, 0.5) | 2. Call configure(kp=NaN, ki=4, kd=1) | 3. Read status, gains(), integral(), configured() | 4. Call update(3, 0.5)
expected_result: configure returns InvalidConfig; gains() still equals kp=2 ki=4 kd=1; integral() still equals 8; configured() is true; the update returns Ok with output 20
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, gains(), integral(), output
notes: Unit-level analogue only: the design adds no MAVLink or command path (4.3), and configure() is the only gain-setting entry. A rejected malformed value changes no controller state. MAVLink parsing, source, and unsupported-command rejection are owned by the COM stories, not this unit.

title: Given a never-configured Pid, update returns NotConfigured with output 0 and changes no state
preconditions: Freshly constructed Pid, configure never called
inputs: error 1; dt_s=0.5
steps: 1. Construct Pid | 2. Read configured() | 3. Call update(1, 0.5) | 4. Read integral()
expected_result: configured() is false; update returns status NotConfigured with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_FALSE on configured(); EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Unwired default is unusable (design 4.3). The caller must not treat output 0 as a usable command; inhibit enforcement is owned by SAF. Assumes members are default-initialised (design does not state it); confirm in implementation review.

title: Given dt equal to zero or negative zero, update returns InvalidDt with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: dt_s=0 and dt_s=-0; error 1
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(1, 0) | 3. Call update(1, -0.0) | 4. Read integral()
expected_result: Both updates return InvalidDt with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Boundary dt <= 0 (design 4.2 step 2). FR-041 partial: only local rejection; input gating owned by CTL-03 (TC-CTRL-004).

title: Given a negative dt, update returns InvalidDt with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: dt_s=-0.5; error 1
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(1, -0.5) | 3. Read integral()
expected_result: update returns InvalidDt with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Design 4.2 step 2.

title: Given a non-finite dt, update returns InvalidDt with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: dt_s = NaN, +infinity, -infinity; error 1
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(1, NaN) | 3. Call update(1, +infinity) | 4. Call update(1, -infinity) | 5. Read integral()
expected_result: All three updates return InvalidDt with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Design 4.2 step 2. Maximum accepted dt: TBD (design decision), DSN-02 / OD-005, so no upper-bound case.

title: Given the smallest positive normal dt, update accepts it
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=0, kd=0
inputs: dt_s = smallest positive normal float (std::numeric_limits<float>::min()); error 3
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=0, kd=0) | 2. Call update(3, smallest positive normal float)
expected_result: status is Ok; output equals 6
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output
notes: Lower side of the dt boundary: any dt > 0 is accepted. ki=0 and kd=0 keep the I and D terms finite.

title: Given a non-finite error, update returns InvalidInput with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: error = NaN, +infinity, -infinity; dt_s=0.5
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1) | 2. Call update(NaN, 0.5) | 3. Call update(+infinity, 0.5) | 4. Call update(-infinity, 0.5) | 5. Read integral()
expected_result: All three updates return InvalidInput with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Local last-line-of-defence rejection (design 4.3). Gating and the safe output for invalid inputs are owned by CTL-03 (TC-CTRL-004).

title: Given a P, I, or D term that overflows, update returns NumericFault with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Freshly constructed Pid; each sub-check configures its own gains
inputs: (a) kp=max float, ki=0, kd=0, error 2, dt_s=0.5; (b) kp=0, ki=max float, kd=0, error 4, dt_s=0.5; (c) kp=0, ki=0, kd=max float, first update(0, 0.5) then update(1, 0.5)
steps: 1. For (a): configure, call update(2, 0.5), read integral() | 2. For (b): configure, call update(4, 0.5), read integral() | 3. For (c): configure, call update(0, 0.5), then update(1, 0.5), then update(1, 1) | 4. Record statuses and outputs
expected_result: (a) and (b): NumericFault, output 0, integral() equals 0; (c): second call returns NumericFault with output 0; third call returns Ok with output equal to max float (so prev_error was not advanced by the rejected call)
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: FR-042 partial: only non-finite results are rejected here; limits and anti-windup are owned by CTL-02 (TC-CTRL-001, TC-CTRL-003). max float is std::numeric_limits<float>::max().

title: Given each term finite but the sum overflowing, update returns NumericFault with output 0 and no state change
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=max float, ki=max float, kd=0
inputs: error 1; dt_s=1
steps: 1. Construct Pid and configure(kp=max float, ki=max float, kd=0) | 2. Call update(1, 1) | 3. Read integral()
expected_result: update returns NumericFault with output 0; integral() equals 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status, output, integral()
notes: Design 4.2 step 5 checks p + i_new + d, not only each term.

title: Given rejected updates of every kind, the next accepted update matches a run in which the rejected calls never happened
preconditions: Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1 and one step applied (error 1, dt_s=0.5; integral 2)
inputs: rejected calls: update(1, 0), update(NaN, 0.5), update(1, NaN); then update(3, 0.5)
steps: 1. Construct Pid, configure(kp=2, ki=4, kd=1), call update(1, 0.5) | 2. Call update(1, 0), update(NaN, 0.5), update(1, NaN) | 3. Read integral() | 4. Call update(3, 0.5)
expected_result: The three rejected calls return InvalidDt, InvalidInput, InvalidDt with output 0; integral() equals 2; the last update returns Ok with output 18
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on statuses, integral(), and final output
notes: B6. The output 18 equals step 2 of TC-CTRL-013.

title: Given several invalid conditions at once, update reports the first failing check in the design order
preconditions: One unconfigured Pid and one Pid configured with kp=2, ki=4, kd=1
inputs: dt_s=0 with error NaN; dt_s=0.5 with error NaN
steps: 1. On the unconfigured Pid call update(NaN, 0) | 2. On the configured Pid call update(NaN, 0) | 3. On the configured Pid call update(NaN, 0.5)
expected_result: Step 1 returns NotConfigured; step 2 returns InvalidDt; step 3 returns InvalidInput; all outputs equal 0
evidence: gtest EXPECT_EQ on status and output
notes: Order is configured, then dt, then error (design 4.2 steps 1 to 3). Pins the order only because the design states it as the algorithm.
